facts.content: Patient presents with sore, cracked, itchy skin on the hands, especially the palms, for 3 to 4 months.
facts.source_text: CC: Sore, cracked, itchy skin on hands, esp. palms, x3-4 months

facts.content: The hand skin symptoms have worsened recently and are interfering with the patient's work as a housekeeper.
facts.source_text: Worse recently; interfering with work (housekeeper); off work x3 days

facts.content: The patient has been off work for 3 days due to the hand symptoms.
The skin on the hands sometimes bleeds with scratching.
The patient has mild dryness on the legs in addition to the hand symptoms.
The patient denies fever, gastrointestinal, or genitourinary symptoms.
facts.source_text: Denies fever, GI, or GU sx

facts.content: The patient tried E45 and antihistamines for the skin symptoms with no effect.
The patient has no history of eczema or dermatitis.
facts.source_text: No hx of eczema or dermatitis

facts.content: Patient has a history of diabetes.
Patient is taking metformin.
Patient has no known allergies.
There is a family history of diabetes.
The patient works as a hotel housekeeper with frequent exposure to cleaning products and does not always wear gloves.
facts.source_text: SH: Housekeeper (hotel); frequent exposure to cleaning products, not always wears gloves

facts.content: The patient does not smoke.
The patient reports minimal alcohol use of a couple of pints per week.
No physical examination or vital signs are documented.
Diagnosed with hand dermatitis, likely contact in nature, based on sore, cracked, itchy palms, occupational exposure, and poor response to over-the-counter emollient and antihistamine.
facts.source_text: 1. Hand dermatitis (likely contact) — Sore, cracked, itchy palms; occupational exposure; poorly responsive to OTC emollient/antihistamine

facts.content: Diabetes is assessed as stable per history.
Patient is advised to wear gloves for all cleaning and laundry tasks.
facts.source_text: Advise gloves with all cleaning/laundry tasks

facts.content: Topical steroid cream is prescribed for the skin condition.
Stronger emollients are prescribed to be applied 3 to 4 times per day.
The prescription is sent to the pharmacy.
Patient is advised to follow up if not improved in 10 to 14 days or if symptoms are worsening.
facts.source_text: F/U if not improved in 10-14 days or if worsening
